question: Your customer support agent's system prompt tells it to call escalate_to_human whenever a message contains the word charge or billing. The tool descriptions clearly state that process_refund handles in-policy refunds such as duplicate charges. Logs show that simple duplicate-charge requests are escalated instead of refunded, which lowers first-contact resolution. The team agrees to rewrite the instruction. Which rewrite best fixes the routing while keeping valid escalations?

options.text: Move the charge and billing keyword rule out of the system prompt and into the escalate_to_human tool description so that it sits beside the tool.
options.reason: The rule still ties words to one tool. It also makes the escalate_to_human description overlap with process_refund, so duplicate-charge requests are still escalated.

options.text: Change the trigger so that the agent escalates billing messages only when the customer's wording shows strong frustration, anger, or impatience with the support process.
options.reason: The guide says sentiment is an unreliable proxy for case complexity. This rule still escalates simple refunds from upset customers and can miss explicit requests for a human.

options.text: Add the words dispute, invoice, and payment to the trigger list so that the instruction catches every billing request that reaches the agent.
options.reason: A longer keyword list is still a keyword-sensitive instruction. It overrides the process_refund description for even more in-policy requests, so misrouting gets worse.

options.text: Replace the keyword trigger with escalation conditions, such as an explicit request for a human or a policy gap, and let the tool descriptions route other requests.
options.reason: Removing the keyword-sensitive instruction stops it from overriding the well-written descriptions, so duplicate charges reach process_refund. Condition-based criteria keep the escalations that are actually needed.
